title: bug: JetBrains keeps a confirmed downgrade after the project re-declares verified-local in the same session, so a later legacy declaration runs legacy after restart with no new confirmation
description:
Found by CQ-RF07 (task-f3f364a6), the epic-final adversarial review. RF02's QA (task-f3485ac9 reviewSummary) noted it as a candidate for epic-final hardening.

Evidence at 28df02f7, RuntimeSelectionPolicy.profile(): `if (key in pinned) return PROTECTED` runs before declaresVerifiedLocal. After a human clicks Allow Downgrade (askDowngrade persists LEGACY), a verified-local declaration later in the same JVM session never re-persists PROTECTED. If the repository then flips back to legacy before the restart, the next session reads LEGACY with no prompt. A related case: the dialog's answer is applied without re-reading the declaration, so an Allow clicked after the project already re-declares verified-local still persists LEGACY.

Impact is narrow: a human allowed legacy once. But the repository's later verified-local declaration is lost, so a second downgrade happens without the confirmation the epic rail requires.

Fix direction: on a pinned key, still note a verified-local read and persist PROTECTED when the stored record is not PROTECTED; in the confirmation callback, persist LEGACY only if the declaration is still weaker.
definitionOfDone: After a confirmed downgrade, a verified-local declaration in the same session re-records PROTECTED, so a later weaker declaration asks again after restart; an Allow applied when the project already re-declares verified-local persists nothing.
Existing RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest rows (D1-D12, PS1-PS8) pass unchanged; new rows fail on 28df02f7 and pass after the fix.
`cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun"` exits 0 under the jetbrains-gradle lease.

implementationPlan.description:

D13: `D13 a verified-local read after an allowed downgrade records protected again, so a later weaker declaration asks after restart`.
1. profileOf(dir) is PROTECTED and records protected.
2. writeProfile(dir, 'legacy'), then forgetSessionForTest(). profileOf is PROTECTED and asks once. asks.answers.single()(true) records legacy.
3. writeProjectJson(dir, '{'). profileOf is PROTECTED and the record stays legacy: an unreadable declaration records nothing, as D4 expects.
4. writeProfile(dir, 'verified-local'). profileOf is PROTECTED, and the record now equals profileJson(dir, 'protected'). This assertion fails today, because a pinned key returns before the declaration is read.
5. writeProfile(dir, 'legacy'). profileOf is PROTECTED, and there is no second ask this session (asks.paths.size == 1).
6. forgetSessionForTest() (a restart). profileOf is PROTECTED and asks again: asks.paths == [dir.path, dir.path]. Today it answers LEGACY with no ask.

D14: `D14 an Allow answered after the project re-declares verified-local, or while project.json is unreadable, records nothing`.
1. profileOf(dir) records protected. Then, for each later declaration in ['{"settings":{"executionProfile":"verified-local"}}', '{']:
   - writeProfile(dir, 'legacy'), then forgetSessionForTest();
   - profileOf is PROTECTED, with one more ask;
   - writeProjectJson(dir, later), then asks.answers.last()(true);
   - the record still equals profileJson(dir, 'protected').
   Today the first case records legacy.
2. Windows only: return@withProfileStore when !windowsHost, as D8 does. This part checks that the matched spellings stay untouched too.
   - Set up as D8 does: base = <newFolder b>/proj and local = <newFolder a>/proj, both declaring legacy.
   - store.write(localName, profileJson(local, 'protected')).
   - RuntimeSelectionPolicy.sameDirectory = { stored, _ -> stored == Paths.get(key(local)) }.
   - profileOf(base) is PROTECTED and asks for base.path.
   - writeProfile(base, 'verified-local'), then asks.answers.last()(true).
   - store.read(localName) is still profileJson(local, 'protected'), and base has no record (assertNull).
   Today both get recorded legacy.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt (DoD 1).

(1) Add `private val recordLock = Any()` with a one-line comment. Every record-write decision runs under it: a verified-local read's PROTECTED record, and an Allow's LEGACY records. A re-declaration seen after an Allow then always leaves PROTECTED.

(2) Reorder profile():
- Read the declaration first. On a failure, return PROTECTED exactly as today: log and fail closed, with no pin and no write.
- If verifiedLocal: `pinned += key`, then `synchronized(recordLock) { if (storedProfile(basePath, key) != StoredProfile.PROTECTED) persist(basePath, key, RuntimeProfile.PROTECTED) }`, then return PROTECTED. This now runs on a pinned key too, with the same single store read the unpinned path does today.
- Next, `if (key in pinned) return RuntimeProfile.PROTECTED`, before any store read, as today.
- Then the existing legacy-like path, unchanged: stored, weaker, aliases, ask.

(3) askDowngrade's callback becomes `if (answered.compareAndSet(false, true) && allow) synchronized(recordLock) { if (stillWeaker(basePath)) { persist the key LEGACY; persist the aliases LEGACY } }`.
- Add a private stillWeaker(basePath) that returns `!declaresVerifiedLocal(...)`. It catches Exception, logs with describe(ex) and returns false: an unreadable declaration keeps the record.
- The first answer still consumes `answered`, so only the first answer counts (D4).
- ProfileDowngradeDialog answers on a pooled thread (executeOnPooledThread) and ask() never blocks. So the lock is never held across confirmer.ask, and the IO stays off the EDT.

(4) Update the `pinned` comment and the object's KDoc to say two things:
- a verified-local read later in the session withdraws an allowed downgrade;
- an Allow downgrades only a declaration that is still weaker when it is answered.

Error handling:
- persist already swallows and logs store failures.
- storedProfile maps any failure to UNTRUSTED, which is not PROTECTED, so a verified-local read rewrites it, as the unpinned path does today.
- Nothing new can throw out of profile() or the callback.

Behaviour that must not change:
- A malformed declaration gives PROTECTED with no pin and no write (D4).
- Concurrent first reads produce one ask (D1).
- In D6's delayed reader, the legacy path calls store() in the same order.

Cost: a pinned project now reads project.json (strict, at most 1 MiB) on every call, and only a verified-local read also reads the store. Unpinned legacy projects already pay both reads.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: RuntimeSelectionPolicy.profile() records PROTECTED whenever it reads a verified-local declaration, including for a project already pinned this session. A downgrade allowed earlier in the session therefore stops standing once the repository re-declares verified-local, and a later weaker declaration asks again after the restart. The downgrade dialog's Allow writes LEGACY, for the project and its matched spellings, only if the declaration is still weaker when it is answered. If the declaration is verified-local or unreadable at answer time, the Allow writes nothing. Record decisions and writes are serialized, so an Allow and a verified-local read never interleave.
acceptanceCriteria: D13: after an allowed downgrade, a verified-local read records protected again, there is no second ask in the session, and the project asks again after a restart once it declares legacy.

D14: an Allow answered after a verified-local re-declaration, or while project.json is unreadable, leaves the record protected. On Windows, the matched spelling's protected record is untouched and the base gets no record.
D13 and D14 fail on the current code, and D1-D12 and PS1-PS8 pass unchanged.

recordLock is never held across confirmer.ask.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Keep the pinned early return and add a second declaration read inside it: rejected, because it duplicates the read and its failure handling. Reordering is smaller. (2) Cache 'recorded PROTECTED this session' to skip the store read: rejected. The Allow path would have to invalidate it, and it goes stale if another IDE on the same store changes the record. (3) Record PROTECTED for an unreadable declaration on a pinned key: rejected, because it diverges from the unpinned fail-closed semantics that D4 pins. (4) No lock: rejected. An Allow could write LEGACY after a verified-local read had written PROTECTED, which loses the re-declaration.
